artifact.title: Data Center Energy Industry Update – Houston, TX (November 2, 2026)
artifact.summary: iMasons Texas Local Chapter co-hosted a one-day executive conference in Houston on November 2, 2026, uniting energy producers, equipment manufacturers, and AI data center developers focused on the South Central U.S. market. The agenda covered ERCOT large load updates, power procurement, generation and load forecasts, and debottlenecking power for AI infrastructure.

artifact.title: ERCOT's Large Load Queue Has Nearly Quadrupled in a Single Year to 226 GW
artifact.summary: ERCOT's large load interconnection queue reached approximately 226 GW as of November 2026, nearly quadrupling from 63 GW at end-2024, with roughly 77% of that demand attributable to data centers targeting grid connection by 2030. Texas Governor Abbott signed a law in July 2026 directing the PUC to create new transparency requirements for large-load customers and cost-allocation reforms, with rulemaking due by December 2026.

artifact.title: US Data Centre Boom Adds 54 GW to Pipeline, Raising RE Demand
artifact.summary: The US data centre development pipeline expanded by 54 GW in the second quarter of 2026, marking a 29% increase year-on-year as developers accelerated construction amid growing concerns over power availability, according to a new report by Wood Mackenzie. The expansion is expected to intensify the focus on electricity supply, grid infrastructure and clean energy procurement as data centres emerge as a major source of incremental power demand in the US. The cumulative disclosed data centre pipeline has crossed 430 GW, with around 59% of the capacity under active development. Nearly 80 GW of projects were under construction, up from 44 GW at the end of the first quarter, Wood Mackenzie said in its US data centre pipeline report. The pipeline added 5% capacity quarter-on-quarter. Meanwhile, utility commitments backed by signed electricity service or construction agreements reached 201 GW, equivalent to 26% of projected US peak electricity demand in 2026. However, the rapid expansion is facing mounting opposition from local communities and lawmakers. More than 400 data centre moratoriums have been introduced across 42 states since January 2026, affecting 18% of tracked sites and putting more than 100 GW of planned capacity under scrutiny. “The latest data reveals projects are steadily advancing from early development to permitting and construction phases,” said Caitlin Connelly, senior analyst at Wood Mackenzie. signals.faradays_take: Texas issued at least 16 data center permits after Governor Abbott's September 21 moratorium directive, revealing regulatory compliance gaps. Following watchdog pressure, TCEQ suspended those permits and is shutting down its automatic filing system pending ERCOT's grid-and-water audit due December 10.

artifact.title: Despite Abbott Moratorium, Texas Kept on Issuing Data Center Permits. Now the State Agency Is Shutting Down Its Automatic Filing System.
artifact.summary: An investigation found that at least 16 data center permits were issued by TCEQ after Governor Abbott's September 21 directive ordering all data center permitting halted pending an ERCOT grid-and-water audit, exposing a compliance gap. Following watchdog scrutiny by Public Citizen and FracTracker, TCEQ announced it is suspending those permits and shutting down its automatic filing system; ERCOT is not expected to deliver audit findings until December 10.

signals.faradays_take: Modo Energy reports 92 GW of data center capacity in advanced planning stages across ERCOT requesting grid access as of October 2026, plus 11 GW in expansion projects. Development is concentrated in DFW, West Texas, the Panhandle, and Central Texas I-35 Corridor, with AI leases financing construction and electricity demand ramping.

artifact.title: Modo Energy: ERCOT Data Center Buildout Forecast – October 2026
artifact.summary: As of October 21, 2026, Modo Energy tracks 92 GW of advanced-planning data center load requesting grid access in ERCOT, with an additional 11 GW of expansion projects, spanning development corridors from Dallas–Fort Worth into West Texas, the Panhandle, and the Central Texas I-35 Corridor. Long-term AI leases are financing construction, with electricity demand ramping as developers connect to the grid and install computing equipment.

signals.faradays_take: ERCOT reported 438 GW of large-load requests in May 2026 dominated by data centers, with interconnection queue wait times reaching 12 years in congested regions. Queue position has become the critical bottleneck for AI infrastructure deployment across U.S. ISOs.

artifact.title: Interconnection Queues Explained: Why New Power Waits Years — 2026 Data Center Update
artifact.summary: ERCOT VP Jeff Billo reported at a late-May 2026 board presentation that large-load requests totaled 438 GW — nearly equal to the 452 GW of generation requests — with data centers comprising the vast majority; large-load processes across all ISOs are being rewritten in 2026. Worst-case interconnection wait times for data centers can reach up to 12 years in congested regions, reinforcing that queue position has become the scarcest asset in U.S. AI infrastructure siting.

signals.faradays_take: Texas Governor Abbott issued a September 21 directive to pause data center permit approvals, but environmental nonprofits discovered the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality continued processing permit-related activities despite the stated halt. Abbott's office claims no new permits were formally approved, though the contradiction raises questions about permit processing transparency.

artifact.title: 'It Ain't Right:' Texas Said It Would Halt Data Center Permits. The State is Pushing Ahead Anyway
artifact.summary: Despite Governor Abbott's September 21 directive pausing data center permit approvals pending review by multiple state agencies, nonprofits Public Citizen and FracTracker Alliance found that the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality had continued processing permit-related activities at data center sites. Abbott's office denied that any new permits had been formally approved, stating that no state agency will act until the PUC, ERCOT, and Water Development Board have sufficient information.

signals.faradays_take: Analysis of regional power grid interconnection queues shows ERCOT leading with 474 GW of data center requests (90% of queue) at 4.79× peak load ratio, NYISO with 12,670 MW across 51 projects, and CAISO projecting 1.8-4.9 GW data center growth through 2040. FERC initiated six large-load proceedings in June 2026, indicating intensifying regulatory scrutiny of data center power demands.

artifact.title: Data Center Power Demand and Grid Queues by Region, 2026
artifact.summary: A nine-region comparison using LBNL Queued Up data shows ERCOT tracking approximately 474 GW of large-load requests as of June 2026 (roughly 90% data centers) and having the largest queue relative to peak load at 4.79×, while NYISO counted 51 large-load projects totaling nearly 12,670 MW by May 2026. FERC opened six large-load proceedings in June 2026, and CAISO's CEC forecast projects data center load growth of 1.8 GW by 2030 and 4.9 GW by 2040.

artifact.title: Data Centers in Texas Statistics 2026: Grid, Tax and Water
artifact.summary: ERCOT's large-load interconnection queue reached approximately 474 GW by June 2026—about 90% data centers—up from 232 GW at end of 2025, representing roughly 5.5 times ERCOT's all-time peak demand. On August 3, 2026, Governor Abbott directed PUCT and ERCOT to audit all data centers advancing through the interconnection process, and ERCOT simultaneously paused its Batch Zero study to verify eligibility of large loads.

artifact.title: How Data Centers Are Rewriting Homeowners' Property Tax and Power Bills in 2026 (ABC17 / Ownwell)
artifact.summary: Virginia's two-year state budget effective June 29, 2026 imposed a statewide electricity consumption tax on data centers of $0.011 per kilowatt-hour expected to generate up to $600 million annually, while Illinois Governor Pritzker paused processing of data center incentive applications for two years starting July 1, citing energy affordability and water use. Texas Governor Abbott ordered an audit of data center grid connections on August 3, 2026, with ERCOT facing roughly 474 gigawatts of connection requests — approximately 90% from data centers.

artifact.title: California Links Data Center Permitting And Licensing To New Water Use Disclosure And Drought Planning Obligations
artifact.summary: California's newly enacted AB 2469 and AB 2619 impose water-supply assessments, efficiency reporting, and drought contingency planning obligations that fundamentally reshape data center permitting; separately, Texas Governor Abbott ordered TCEQ to halt all data center permit issuance until ERCOT completes a grid and water-resource audit. These actions reflect an accelerating national trend of states requiring data centers to internalize water infrastructure costs.

artifact.title: Texas Pauses Certain Data Center Approvals Amid Grid, Water, and Community Concerns
artifact.summary: Texas has effectively halted new data center approvals through both the ERCOT interconnection process and TCEQ permitting: Governor Abbott's August 3 ERCOT audit directive was followed on September 21 by a TCEQ permit freeze for all data centers until ERCOT's audit is complete. The dual-agency pause creates compounding uncertainty for projects across the state.

signals.faradays_take: ERCOT's interconnection queue surged from 63 GW to 410 GW between December 2024 and March 2026, with 87% driven by AI data center demand. artifact.title: Texas ERCOT Market and Large-Load Connections for AI Data Centers
artifact.summary: ERCOT's large-load interconnection queue grew from 63 GW in December 2024 to 410 GW by March 2026, with roughly 87% attributable to AI data centers—a transformation the PUCT is addressing through a suite of SB 6 rulemakings finalized in September–October 2026. Key new rules include mandatory $50,000/MW financial security postings, mandatory curtailment for any large load connecting on or after January 1, 2026, and formal interconnection standards under 16 TAC §25.194, with transmission cost allocation rules due by December 31, 2026.

signals.faradays_take: Regulatory analysis of large-load grid connection procedures across seven major U.S. ISOs for AI data centers in 2026, detailing PJM's five-pillar program and ERCOT's PGRR145 Batch Zero launch with pause for eligibility verification. artifact.title: Large Load Grid Connection and Study Agreements for AI Data Centers
artifact.summary: A comprehensive review of how PJM, ERCOT, MISO, SPP, CAISO, ISO-NE, and NYISO each handle large-load interconnection for AI data centers in 2026, including PJM's January 2026 decisional letter establishing a five-pillar large-load program and ERCOT's PGRR145 Batch Zero launch (effective July 11, 2026, then paused August 3, 2026 for eligibility verification). The piece highlights that existing surplus interconnect rights have become arguably the scarcest asset class in U.S. power.

signals.faradays_take: PJM and MISO face severe interconnection queue delays exceeding 8 years, with PJM managing 260+ GW of requests and ERCOT seeing 198 GW of large load applications in Q1 2026, predominantly from data centers. artifact.title: MISO and PJM Interconnection Queue Delays for Data Centers
artifact.summary: As of late 2025/early 2026, PJM's average interconnection timeline has stretched past eight years, with the queue carrying more than 260 GW of requests and PJM logging 95 large-load adjustment requests totaling ~54 GW through November 2025. In ERCOT, 198 GW of large load applied for interconnection in Q1 2026 alone, with data centers accounting for the vast majority, while PJM faces a potential 15 GW capacity shortfall by 2030.

artifact.title: Texas Pauses All Environmental Permitting for Data Centers
artifact.summary: On September 21, 2026, Texas Governor Greg Abbott directed the TCEQ to halt issuance of all environmental permits for data centers until ERCOT completes an audit of grid and water resource impacts. The directive extends state scrutiny to environmental permitting, water consumption, noise, light, traffic, and financial assistance disclosures, creating broad uncertainty for new and in-process Texas data center projects.

signals.faradays_take: Regulatory analysis comparing demand response and curtailment frameworks across DOE, PJM, ERCOT, and FERC shows AI data center curtailment thresholds ranging from 20-75 MW, with expedited interconnection pathways for voluntary participation. FERC's April 2026 decision preserves state-level control over demand response aggregation opt-outs.

artifact.title: Demand Response and Curtailment for Large AI Data Centers
artifact.summary: A detailed regulatory comparison across DOE, PJM, ERCOT, and FERC Order 2222 frameworks shows that curtailment thresholds for AI data centers range from 20 MW (DOE ANOPR) to 75 MW (ERCOT), with expedited 60-day interconnection studies offered to loads that voluntarily agree to be curtailable. In April 2026, FERC withdrew its inquiry on removing the state opt-out for demand response aggregations, leaving a key flexibility mechanism to states.

artifact.title: Texas Cuts the Data Center Grid Deposit From $100,000 to $50,000 per MW During Its Own Queue Pause

The commission also extended how long a stalled project retains its queue position, during a pause triggered by queue saturation.

The action represents a significant regulatory reversal for a state that had previously offered generous economic development incentives to attract data center investment.

artifact.title: Texas Cuts the Data Center Grid Deposit From $100,000 to $50,000 per MW During Its Own Queue Pause
artifact.summary: The Public Utility Commission of Texas voted in September 2026 to adopt large load interconnection standards for ERCOT, halving the financial security deposit from $100,000 to $50,000 per MW of requested peak demand and eliminating a proposed non-refundable $50,000/MW interconnection fee. The rules apply to loads with peak demand over 75 MW and replaced tiered study fees with a flat $100,000 study fee for all large load customers.

State-level moratorium bills have been introduced in 11 states in 2026, while Texas has chosen regulatory cost-allocation over construction pauses.

The report projects that national deliveries could fall by half in 2028, concentrated in PJM and ERCOT markets where grid interconnection processes are being redesigned.

artifact.title: Interconnection Queue Tracker 2026 — ERCOT, PJM, MISO, SPP
artifact.summary: A live tracker of large-load interconnection queues across seven US ISOs shows approximately 226 GW queued in ERCOT and ~800 projects totaling ~55 GW targeted for PJM by 2030, with data center share growing rapidly in Northern Virginia, Texas, and Chicago markets. The tracker highlights where geographic and queue-position constraints most acutely affect data center time-to-power calculations.

signals.faradays_take: ERCOT is implementing RFI requirements for data center developers with capacity thresholds (≥75 MW for audits, ≥25 MW for community reviews) and strict grid model deadlines under PGRR145. Grid operator interconnection studies and queue rules are critical determinants of data center project timelines and energization eligibility.

artifact.title: Data Center Grid Operator Watchlist: ERCOT, PJM, FERC & Every RTO
artifact.summary: ERCOT is issuing RFIs to data center developers through TSPs/DSPs for Batch Zero eligibility audits (≥75 MW) and community impact reviews (≥25 MW computational loads), with a strict dynamic model data deadline under PGRR145. A data center cannot energize until its grid operator completes interconnection studies, making each operator's queue rules and curtailment conditions the primary determinant of project timelines.
